feed.title: Handling PQ signatures on the stack

entry.title: Handling PQ signatures on the stack
entry.summary:
Upgradable limits in TapScript are intentionally designed to avoid arbitrary restrictions, allowing for future consensus changes without the need to accommodate legacy constraints. Imposing chunking mechanisms is therefore considered unnecessary and counterproductive, as it introduces limitations that could be lifted through protocol upgrades.
Blacklisting opcodes undermines the objective of enabling advanced manipulations of signature data within scripts. By prohibiting certain operations, this method restricts innovative uses of signature data that could otherwise offer new functionalities, essentially stifling potential advancements in script capabilities.
Optimizing implementations by selectively covering anticipated use cases presents risks rather than thoroughness. This approach depends on predicting all possible applications, and any oversight can introduce vulnerabilities, especially if users or real-world transactions depend on scenarios that were neglected during optimization. While optimization may appear appealing due to its intellectual challenges and benefits, it carries the danger of overlooking critical aspects, potentially compromising security.
The variable operations (varops) budget, as proposed by GSR, offers a robust solution for supporting complex scripting with substantial data manipulation. This strategy provides flexibility and scalability, accommodating more sophisticated applications without imposing artificial caps on script complexity.
Utilizing an isolated signature stack stands out as the simplest method for those willing to limit or postpone creative uses of signature data until further solutions like GSR are implemented independently. An isolated stack also opens up the possibility of applying greater transaction fee discounts, as outlined in [this discussion](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/segwit-commitment-to-post-quantum-witness-data/2702), making it an attractive choice for straightforward implementations.
